entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv6625"/><title type="x-s2">PSALM 97</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Ps.97.1-Ps.97.12">Psa 97:1-12</reference>. The writer celebrates the Lord's dominion over nations and nature, describes its effect on foes and friends, and exhorts and encourages the latter.</title> <div sID="gen10145" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv6625"/>1-2. This dominion is a cause of joy, because, even though our minds are oppressed with terror before the throne of the King of kings (<reference osisRef="Exod.19.16">Ex 19:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.5.22">De 5:22</reference>), we know it is based on righteous principles and judgments which are according to truth. <div eID="gen10145" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv6628"/><div sID="gen10148" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv6628"/>7. Idolaters are utterly put to shame, for if angels must worship Him, how much more those who worshipped them.<div eID="gen10148" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen10149" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">all ye gods--</hi>literally, "all ye angels" (<reference osisRef="Ps.8.5">Psa 8:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.138.1">138:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Heb.1.6">He 1:6</reference>; 2:7). Paul quotes, not as a prophecy, but as language used in regard to the Lord Jehovah, who in the Old Testament theophania is the second person of the Godhead. <div eID="gen10149" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv6631"/><div sID="gen10153" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv6631"/>10-12. Let gratitude for the blessings of providence and grace incite saints (<reference osisRef="Ps.4.3">Psa 4:3</reference>) to holy living. Spiritual blessings are in store, represented by light (<reference osisRef="Ps.27.1">Psa 27:1</reference>) and gladness. <div eID="gen10153" type="x-p"/>
